about.heading: Why INOK
body: INOK stands for Idhu Namme Oru Kedai, Tamil for "this is our shop". Every participant came with a business of their own, and every lesson was about growing it.

Small businesses in the Malaysian Indian community often have strong products but little time or support to take them online. INOK was designed to change that: practical digital-marketing skills, taught in person, then applied to each participant's own business with a mentor alongside.

Over six days in Ipoh, participants worked through strategy, content, advertising, AI tools and marketplace selling with practitioners who run these campaigns for a living. They then spent 20 days putting it to work online, with a mentor checking in along the way.

The Program Pensijilan Digital Marketing Strategist was delivered by GET Academy with funding from MITRA, the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit, and certified by SEGi College Subang Jaya, GET Academy's strategic educational partner within SEGi University & Colleges.

curriculum.heading: What participants learned
curriculum.intro: Three strands ran through the six days. Every lesson was taught, demonstrated, then applied to the participant's own business before the session ended, so nobody went home with theory alone.

groups.title: Strategy

modules.title: Digital marketing strategy
modules.text: How online marketing brings in customers, and how to set goals, choose the right channels and measure what works when time and budget are tight.

modules.title: Knowing your target customer
modules.text: Building a customer persona: who buys, where they spend time online, what problem the product solves for them and what makes them act.

modules.title: Business and product positioning
modules.text: What makes their product different, how to say it in one line, and how to present it so it stands out from the competition.

groups.intro: Before any posting, a plan. Participants learned to think like marketers about their own shop.

groups.title: Content and social

modules.title: Video editing with CapCut
modules.text: Shooting and editing short vertical videos on a phone: cuts, captions, music and an opening that holds attention.

modules.title: Social media content
modules.text: Planning what to post and when, writing captions that sell, and recording, publishing and going live on TikTok.

modules.title: Facebook and Instagram marketing
modules.text: Setting up and naming a business page, building a following, and turning followers into customers with posts and stories.

groups.intro: Then the content that does the selling, made on the phone in their pocket.

groups.title: Ads, AI and selling

modules.title: Google Ads
modules.text: How paid search works, how to reach people already searching for what they sell, and how to keep spending under control.

modules.title: ChatGPT for business
modules.text: Using AI as a daily assistant to draft captions, product descriptions, video scripts and content ideas in minutes.

modules.title: Selling on Shopee and Lazada
modules.text: Choosing products, finding suppliers and setting up a marketplace shop, so customers can find and buy beyond the participant's own followers.

groups.intro: Finally, the tools that widen the reach and close the sale.

journey.heading: The 26-day journey

steps.title: Know yourself
steps.text: The programme opened with the fundamentals of digital marketing, then turned straight to the participants themselves. Each one chose the single business they would grow for the rest of the programme and built a persona for it: who runs it, what it sells and why that matters to a customer. Before the day was out, they were editing their first short videos in CapCut, step by step.
steps.takeaway: a clear picture of their own business, and their first edited video.

steps.title: Know your product
steps.text: Participants set up their business pages on Facebook and Instagram, from naming the page to deciding what to post. Trainers then walked them through Google Ads: how paid search works, who sees an ad and what it costs to reach them. The day closed with ChatGPT as a working tool for captions, product descriptions and content ideas.
steps.takeaway: business pages ready to use, and an AI assistant for everyday content.

steps.title: Know your customer
steps.text: The focus moved from the product to the people who buy it. Participants worked out who their customer is and what makes them stop scrolling, then put it into practice: they recorded informational videos and uploaded them to TikTok during the session, with trainers on hand to help.
steps.takeaway: videos published on their own TikTok accounts, made in class.

steps.title: Know your place
steps.text: Day four was about where to show up online and what to say there. Participants learned how to choose TikTok topics that sell, filmed content out on location, and learned to run live-streams: setting up, holding an audience and turning viewers into buyers.
steps.takeaway: a plan for TikTok content, and the confidence to go live.

steps.title: Know your strategy
steps.text: Next came the marketplaces. Participants learned how Shopee and Lazada work for a small seller: choosing products that will sell, finding suppliers they can rely on, and setting up a shop that customers trust.
steps.takeaway: a way to sell online beyond their own followers.

steps.title: Go viral
steps.text: The last classroom day pulled the week together. A viral-marketing challenge put every skill to the test, a hands-on product-branding session showed how presentation sells, and participants ran live selling sessions on TikTok.
steps.takeaway: branding that makes a product stand out, tested live.

steps.title: Mentored implementation
steps.text: Back at their own shops, participants put the plan to work online: posting content, going live and building their pages, with a mentor checking in along the way. This is when the first results came in, from new followers to first online sales.
steps.takeaway: a business that is already working online, not just a plan.

steps.title: Certified
steps.text: Participants who completed the programme received the Certified Professional in Digital Marketing Strategist certificate, issued by SEGi College Subang Jaya, GET Academy's strategic educational partner. Trainees then moved on to paid placements running live digital-marketing projects.

kpis.heading: The brief, and how we delivered it
kpis.intro: INOK was funded against a clear set of outputs and KPIs. Here is each one, the work that delivered it, and the evidence on record.

items.target: Plan, run and evaluate social-media strategies and marketing campaigns
items.how: Six days of strategy modules covering customer personas, Facebook, Instagram, Google Ads, ChatGPT, TikTok and the marketplaces, each one applied to the participant's own business the same day.
items.evidence: daily schedule, signed attendance sheets, photos and day films.

items.target: Hands-on coaching to develop and launch digital tools for the business
items.how: Participants recorded and published their own TikTok videos and ran live sessions in class, and launched portfolio websites for their businesses. One built a complete site within the six days.
items.evidence: published videos, live sessions and portfolio websites.

items.target: Learn entrepreneurship methods: strategy, marketing and operations
items.how: Six modules took each participant from Know Yourself to Know Your Strategy: positioning the business, understanding the customer, choosing products to sell and finding suppliers.
items.evidence: module schedule and participant handover reports.

items.target: Every participant uses e-commerce and digital tools
items.how: TikTok, Shopee, Lazada, CapCut and ChatGPT were taught and practised hands-on in session, on participants' own phones and accounts, not just demonstrated.

items.target: Make products reachable through marketing apps
items.how: Participants created or grew TikTok accounts and launched portfolio websites. One TikTok shop made its first online sales within days of the classroom phase.
items.evidence: participants' account screenshots in the final report.

items.how: Before-and-after quizzes tracked progress in business goals, online presence, customer insight and content creation. Trainees then moved on to paid placements of about six months.

kpis._note: Targets paraphrase the grant's outputs and KPIs (Lampiran C) as set out in the final report's KPI table (section 6); 'how' and 'evidence' follow that table's achievement column. KPI (i) (a participant-count target) is deliberately left out: no participant counts on the page (user decision 2026-11-10). The quiz result count is not shown.
